title: Death of Alexander the Great
summary: Alexander died in Babylon on 10 June 323 BCE (one page gives 10 or 11 June), aged 32, after a fever of about two weeks that began after a party at the home of Medius of Thessaly. He lost the power of speech before dying. The cause is unresolved; poisoning rumours circulated, and his successors then began dividing the empire.

uncertainty.note: WHE states 10 June 323 BCE in the text and "10 or 11 June 323 BCE" in metadata; the NIH paper says June 10, 323 BC. Illness onset is given there as May 29, 323 BC.

where.historical_name: Babylon (WHE: he was moved to his palace there)

importance.justification: Ended Alexander's reign of 336-323 BCE and was followed by the Wars of the Diadochi.

sources.title: Alexander the Great and West Nile Virus Encephalitis
sources.publisher: Emerging Infectious Diseases (CDC) via PubMed Central
sources.author: John S. Marr and Charles H. Calisher

reviewer_note: The day is 10 June on both main pages but WHE metadata allows 11 June. WHE says "palace" without naming it. Pin is the OSM Babylon site. Cause of death is unresolved (the NIH paper proposes West Nile encephalitis; WHE says modern historians generally accept natural causes).
